recipes.name: Scones
ingredients_raw: 3 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for kneading

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Lightly grease a baking sheet.
Combine flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt in a large bowl; cut in butter with 2 knives or a pastry blender until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Whisk milk and egg in a small bowl; gradually stir into flour mixture until moistened.
Turn dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead briefly, 5 or 6 turns.
Pat or roll dough out into a 1/2-inch thick round. Cut into 8 wedge-shaped pieces and place onto the prepared baking sheet.
Bake scones in the preheated oven until golden brown on top, about 15 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Scones
raw_recipe.description: These simple scones are made with basic pantry ingredients and ready to eat in just 30 minutes! Delicious with butter or clotted cream and berry jam.

review.reviewBody: These just turned out wonderful. I used some of the tricks I read and they were perfect. I added two tsp of cinnamon and I put the egg in the measuring cup then added 1/2 milk and 1/2 half and half cream and the dough consistency was perfect. I added raisins and almonds to mine. When I took the dough from the bowl, it was crumbly, but I was able to easly mold it into a dough ball and flatten it and cut it into about 12 good size scones. I also added a bit of lemon zest.... If people had dough that was too wet, they really need to try putting the egg in the measuring cup first, then adding the milk. If you want quick easy scones, this recipe is for you!!! I will make again.

Wonderful! I've added fresh chopped cranberries and orange zest/juice.Orange glaze. I've made pumpkin scones with cinnamon glaze. Every altered recipe using this base has been a hit. To avoid dough being too wet I crack the egg in the measuring cup first, then measure to one cup milk or half & half over the egg. Seems to come out perfect.

Excellent, I changed it up a bit by using egg nog instead of milk and topped it off with brown sugar and toasted almonds. I gave it an egg wash with egg nog and a dash of Christian Brothers brandy. I also toasted the almonds after blanching them for sixty seconds then removed the skins and sliced them.

These came out great and have made multiple times. Little crumbly when mixed but able to knead and roll out although sticks to fingers. Added a teaspoon of cinnamon, used half and half in lieu of milk and added a cup of blueberries and chopped walnuts. Also used slightly softened butter and found easier to mix.

This recipe is very good especially as a base for scones. I divided the dough into 2 to make them into 2 batches of different flavors. I added mini chocolate chips and slivered almonds to one batch. The other I added shredded cheddar cheese. The contrast of the sweet and salty was actually not bad. I will make it again and next time will definitely add less milk, but still mix both the milk and the egg together before adding it up to the dry ingredients. It was just a bit too wet to handle.

I never used 3/4 cup butter for this recipe. I always use 3/4 of a stick of frozen butter (around 1/3 cup or 6 tbsp). I once used a full stick and the dough was really soggy. My favourite adjustment is adding 1 tbsp of poppy seed along with 2 tbsp of lemon zest and 1.5 tbsp of squeezed lemon. I also like using Oat Milk instead of regular milk.

I tried these out just today and they turned out really well. Since I only had 1/2 stick butter (I live in Spain and our sticks here are only 250 g) I substituted the remainder of lipids for 1/4 cup vegetable oil and I needed 1/2 cup more of flour. I read one time that depending on the country, flours could vary. I also added 1 tsp allspice for some fun. The results were fabulous. Breakfast today with the scones and a hint of that allspice was great! It didn't take long at all to whip up. A nice change to bread. Thanks for this recipe!

Very good recipe. For nicely layered scones that pull apart in lovely chunks be sure to dice your softened (not melted) butter into itty bitty bits and sprinkle it into the dry ingredients. Whisk it around to get little globulous butter and flour chunks, then add the mixed milk/egg and kneed with your hands. Don't over work the dough. We like to add shredded cheddar, diced green onion, and little bits of pre-cooked bacon to our scones.
Absolutely delicious.

These scones turned out great. I don't know about what others are saying about needing more flour, the portions were perfect. 

A couple small changes I made: shredded frozen butter so it stays cold, after forming place in the fridge for 15 minutes before baking, and brush the top with heavy cream before placing on the oven. 

This recipe was so simple and made some of the best scones ice ever made. Thanks

this is a good recipe and I use this for all of my scone flavors! Weigh the flour carefully. Also, mix your egg and milk together first, then add slowly to make sure you don't add TOO much liquid, based on how your dough feels as you mix. I use pastry flour and it makes all the difference.

Wife absolutely loves these and says it tastes just like Scotland. Added some cinnamon and raisins this last time. I add about 1/2 cup more flour as part of mixing and kneading and that see,s to get the right consistency. Thanks for sharing this recipe.

Yeast to make recipe. I added raisins and sprinkled some sugar on top. Mind you, you’ll need extra half cup to 1 cup of flour for kneading. The dough came out quite wet, but after kneading and absorbing more flour, it was good.
I'm sure the recipe is fine but I used whole wheat flour and they didn't taste very good. I buttered the pan and the bottoms burned faster that I could silence the smoke alarm. Lol

I love this recipe :) I make these pretty often for me and my brother and they are always great. I will say though that you can definitely make more than 8 scones with it. I usually get close to 16-ish scones though that’s not a complaint. I have added a cup of blueberries, strawberries, and raspberries and they ended up best with the raspberries and blueberries. ❤️
Easy, ingredients most will already have. I halved the batch and made cheese and raisin scones. Great for afternoon tea.
Even my mother, who doesn't normally like scones, said this recipe made the best scones she's ever tried! I also made blueberry compote to go along. They were gone in only a few days!
Brings back sweet memories!
I have made scones many times before and i prefer this recipe. The only difference is i added a tablespoon of lemon juice to the milk and let it sour! Came out beautifully and light!
Added a pinch more sugar and I roll it in balls instead of triangles
Easy to blend and tasty
